sections.title: The letters th
paragraphs: The letters th make two sounds. The main sound is the sound /θ/. You hear it in the word (think) /θɪŋk/, which means to think.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: Put the tip of your tongue lightly between your front teeth. Blow air softly over the tongue without voice for the first sound. Keep the tongue in the same place and add your voice for the second sound. Feel your throat with your hand to sense the buzz.

sections.title: Reading the letters
paragraphs: The letters th make the voiceless sound /θ/ in most everyday words and at the end of words, as in (bath) /bɑːθ/. They make the voiced sound /ð/ in small grammar words like (this) /ðɪs/, and between vowels as in (father) /fɑː.ðə/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not replace these sounds with an s, z, t, or d sound. Keep your tongue right between your front teeth, not behind them. Let the air flow smoothly, without stopping it completely.
